claim: The placenta is the interface between mother and fetus in all eutherian species.
source: The placenta is the interface between mother and fetus in all eutherian species.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about placental function in eutherian mammals.

claim: Syncytial cells of the placenta have made dissociation and independent evaluation of different cell types difficult.
source: A substantial challenge has been the syncytial cells of the placenta, which have made dissociation and independent evaluation of the different cell types of this organ difficult.
evidence: This is stated as a known challenge in the field, representing established knowledge about technical difficulties in placental research.

claim: Single nuclei RNA sequencing was performed at multiple stages of mouse embryonic development focusing on the labyrinth.
source: Here, we address questions concerning the ontogeny, specification, and function of the cell types of a representative hemochorial placenta by performing single nuclei RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) at multiple stages of mouse embryonic development focusing on the exchange interface, the labyrinth.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: Analysis by snRNA-seq identified transcript profiles and inferred functions of all but the most highly polyploid cell types of the placenta.
source: Analysis by snRNA-seq identified transcript profiles and inferred functions, cell trajectories, signaling interactions, and transcriptional drivers of all but the most highly polyploid cell types of the placenta.
evidence: This summarizes the findings from the snRNA-seq analysis performed in the study.

claim: The mouse placenta is separated into three main regions: the decidua, the junctional zone, and the labyrinth.
source: The mouse placenta is separated into three main regions – the decidua, the junctional zone (JZ), and the labyrinth.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about mouse placental structure.

claim: Select fetal trophoblast invade into the maternal decidua and remodel and line maternal arteries.
source: Select fetal trophoblast invade into the maternal decidua and remodel and line maternal arteries, facilitating maternal blood to flow into the fetal portion of the placenta (Adamson et al., 2002; Maltepe and Fisher, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The junctional zone consists of parietal trophoblast giant cells, spongiotrophoblast, and glycogen cells that largely function in hormone secretion and metabolism.
source: The JZ lies directly beneath the decidua and consists of parietal trophoblast giant cells, spongiotrophoblast, and glycogen cells that largely function in hormone secretion and metabolism (Simmons et al., 2007; Woods et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature describing junctional zone composition and function.

claim: The labyrinth is specially designed to maximize surface area for gas and nutrient exchange between maternal and fetal blood.
source: Beneath the JZ, closest to the embryo, is the labyrinth, which is specially designed to maximize surface area for gas and nutrient exchange between maternal and fetal blood (Figure 1A; Simmons et al., 2008a; Soncin et al., 2015; Woods et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations and reference to Figure 1A showing placental structure.

claim: The development of the labyrinth structure begins with fusion of the allantois with the chorion at E8.5.
source: The development of the labyrinth structure begins with fusion of the allantois with the chorion at E8.5 (Cross et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Fusion of the allantois with the chorion begins a process of invasion and branching morphogenesis resulting in an expansive surface area for gas and nutrient exchange by E10.5.
source: This begins a process of invasion and branching morphogenesis resulting in an expansive surface area for gas and nutrient exchange by E10.5 (Soncin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The gas exchange interface in the mouse contains three layers of differentiated trophoblast separating maternal blood from the endothelial cells of the fetal vasculature.
source: The gas exchange interface in the mouse contains three layers of differentiated trophoblast separating maternal blood from the endothelial cells of the fetal vasculature (Simmons et al., 2008a; Maltepe and Fisher, 2015; Coan et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature describing the structure of the gas exchange interface.

claim: Sinusoidal trophoblast giant cells reside in the maternal blood space and have demonstrated exocrine functions.
source: Sinusoidal trophoblast giant cells (S-TGC) reside in the maternal blood space, have demonstrated exocrine functions, and are a source of placental lactogens (Simmons et al., 2008b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: S-TGC are perforated allowing maternal blood to contact SynTI.
source: S-TGC are attached to the outermost syncytiotrophoblast layer (SynTI) but are perforated allowing maternal blood to contact SynTI (Coan et al., 2005; Woods et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The two SynT layers together transport gasses and nutrients from the maternal blood to the fetal vasculature.
source: Next, are the two SynT layers which together transport gasses and nutrients from the maternal blood to the fetal vasculature (Georgiades et al., 2002; Woods et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SynTI is the outer layer in direct contact with maternal blood forming the barrier between maternal blood and fetal tissue.
source: SynTI is the outer layer in direct contact with maternal blood forming the barrier between maternal blood and fetal tissue.
evidence: This describes the anatomical position and function of SynTI based on established knowledge.

claim: SynTII functions as an intermediary between SynTI on its apical membrane and the fetal endothelium on its basal side.
source: Beneath, is SynTII which functions as an intermediary between SynTI on its apical membrane and the fetal endothelium on its basal side.
evidence: This describes the anatomical position and function of SynTII based on established knowledge.

claim: Human SynT are 80–200 µM in diameter and contain 5–15 nuclei.
source: As a reference, human SynT are 80–200 µM in diameter and contain 5–15 nuclei meaning their size and fragility do not allow for profiling by FACS or passage through microfluidic channels for droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature describing human SynT characteristics.

claim: Human SynT size and fragility do not allow for profiling by FACS or passage through microfluidic channels for droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing.
source: As a reference, human SynT are 80–200 µM in diameter and contain 5–15 nuclei meaning their size and fragility do not allow for profiling by FACS or passage through microfluidic channels for droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited physical characteristics of human SynT.

claim: Several studies in mouse have profiled the placenta using scRNA-seq.
source: Several studies in both mouse (Nelson et al., 2016; Home and Ghosh, 2019) and human (Vento-Tormo et al., 2018; Suryawanshi et al., 2018) have profiled the placenta using scRNA-seq, however, syncytiotrophoblast are greatly underrepresented in these data.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous scRNA-seq studies.

claim: Syncytiotrophoblast are greatly underrepresented in previous scRNA-seq data of the placenta.
source: Several studies in both mouse (Nelson et al., 2016; Home and Ghosh, 2019) and human (Vento-Tormo et al., 2018; Suryawanshi et al., 2018) have profiled the placenta using scRNA-seq, however, syncytiotrophoblast are greatly underrepresented in these data.
evidence: This is an assessment of previous studies cited in the text.

claim: Studies in mouse have either avoided profiling the labyrinth trophoblast, or are unable to distinguish between the two SynT layers.
source: Studies in mouse have either avoided profiling the labyrinth trophoblast, or are unable to distinguish between the two SynT layers (Nelson et al., 2016; Home and Ghosh, 2019).
evidence: This is an assessment of previous studies cited in the text.

claim: Application of droplet-based transcriptome profiling to nuclei has been shown to provide high quality data and results which recapitulate those from whole cell scRNA-seq.
source: Recently, application of droplet-based transcriptome profiling to nuclei has been shown to provide high quality data and results which recapitulate those from whole cell scRNA-seq (Habib et al., 2017; Lake et al., 2018; Bakken et al., 2018; Ding et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature demonstrating the validity of snRNA-seq.

claim: A total of 27,326 nuclei passed quality control.
source: A total of 27,326 nuclei passed quality control (between 500 and 4000 unique genes identified and fewer than 0.25% mitochondrial reads), ranging from 4124 to 9485 nuclei across the embryonic days (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental data from the study.

claim: Nuclei passing quality control had between 500 and 4000 unique genes identified and fewer than 0.25% mitochondrial reads.
source: A total of 27,326 nuclei passed quality control (between 500 and 4000 unique genes identified and fewer than 0.25% mitochondrial reads), ranging from 4124 to 9485 nuclei across the embryonic days (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the quality control criteria used in the study.

claim: Clustering of nuclei using the Seurat package identified 26 clusters.
source: Clustering of nuclei using the Seurat package identified 26 clusters, then projected in UMAP expression space allowing for an understanding of the relationship among populations as visualized by proximity (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C; Satija et al., 2015; Butler et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct report of the clustering analysis performed in the study.

claim: Based on general markers, populations were separated into five broad groups: trophoblast, decidual stroma, blood cells, endothelial cells, and fetal mesenchyme.
source: Based on general markers, these populations were separated into five broad groups: trophoblast, decidual stroma, blood cells, endothelial cells, and fetal mesenchyme.
evidence: This is a direct report of the cell type classification based on marker gene analysis.

claim: The maternal decidual stroma was identified by the absence of Xist expression in male embryonic tissue.
source: The maternal decidual stroma was identified by the absence of Xist expression in male embryonic tissue (Figure 1E).
evidence: This describes the method used to identify maternal cells based on X-chromosome inactivation marker expression.

claim: One fetal mesenchyme subgroup expressed markers of pericytes including Acta2.
source: One (clusters 6, 10, and 24) expressed markers of pericytes (e.g. Acta2) and several growth factors including Wnt5b and Pdgfrb that are critical for development and maintenance of vascular populations (Eaton et al., 2020).
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression data from the study and citation to literature about these markers.

claim: Another fetal mesenchyme subgroup expressed Gata4, Kit, and Pdpn.
source: The other (clusters 15 and 19) expressed Gata4, Kit, and Pdpn.
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression data from the study.

claim: Immunofluorescence for PDPN showed the cells to be interstitial with long projections that appear to make contact with PECAM positive fetal endothelial cells.
source: The nature of the cells in this subgroup is unclear, but immunofluorescence for PDPN showed the cells to be interstitial with long projections that appear to make contact with PECAM positive fetal endothelial cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence imaging data from the study.

claim: The endothelial group consisted of cells expressing markers of vascular endothelium (Cluster 3 - Pecam1, Kdr, Tek).
source: The endothelial group consisted of cells expressing markers of vascular endothelium (Cluster 3 - Pecam1, Kdr, Tek), lymphatic endothelium (cluster 26 - Flt4/Vegfr3), and pro-angiogenic and lymphogenic lineages (Clusters 20 and 25 - Vegfc and Igf1, respectively) (Cao et al., 1998; Björndahl et al., 2005).
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression data from the study and citations to literature about these markers.

claim: The endothelial group included cells expressing markers of lymphatic endothelium (cluster 26 - Flt4/Vegfr3).
source: The endothelial group consisted of cells expressing markers of vascular endothelium (Cluster 3 - Pecam1, Kdr, Tek), lymphatic endothelium (cluster 26 - Flt4/Vegfr3), and pro-angiogenic and lymphogenic lineages (Clusters 20 and 25 - Vegfc and Igf1, respectively) (Cao et al., 1998; Björndahl et al., 2005).
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression data from the study and citations to literature about these markers.

claim: Lymphatic endothelium has been discovered in human placenta.
source: The identification of cells expressing lymphatic markers is intriguing because the placenta is not thought to contain lymphatics. However, lymphatic endothelium has been discovered in human and it is possible a similar cell type exists in mouse (Pique-Regi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: It is possible a similar cell type to lymphatic endothelium exists in mouse placenta.
source: The identification of cells expressing lymphatic markers is intriguing because the placenta is not thought to contain lymphatics. However, lymphatic endothelium has been discovered in human and it is possible a similar cell type exists in mouse (Pique-Regi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is speculation based on the discovery of lymphatic markers in the mouse data and previous findings in human.

claim: The blood cell group consisted of putative erythrocytes (Cluster 13 - Hbb-y, Hba-x).
source: The blood cell group consisted of putative erythrocytes (Cluster 13 - Hbb-y, Hba-x), macrophages (Cluster 17 - Mrc1+; Martinez and Gordon, 2014), B-cells (Cluster 21 - Bank1, Btla; Aiba et al., 2006), T-cells (Cluster 22 – Gzmc, Slamf1, Cd84; Griewank et al., 2007, Veillette, 2006), and natural killer cells (Cluster 23 Cd244; Lee et al., 2004).
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression data from the study.

claim: The blood cell group included macrophages (Cluster 17 - Mrc1+).
source: The blood cell group consisted of putative erythrocytes (Cluster 13 - Hbb-y, Hba-x), macrophages (Cluster 17 - Mrc1+; Martinez and Gordon, 2014), B-cells (Cluster 21 - Bank1, Btla; Aiba et al., 2006), T-cells (Cluster 22 – Gzmc, Slamf1, Cd84; Griewank et al., 2007, Veillette, 2006), and natural killer cells (Cluster 23 Cd244; Lee et al., 2004).
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression data from the study and citation to literature about this marker.

claim: snRNA-seq has the sensitivity and specificity to identify the multitude of cell types in the developing placenta.
source: Together, these data show that snRNA-seq has the sensitivity and specificity to identify the multitude of cell types in the developing placenta.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: Trophoblast cells make up the largest of the five broad groups of nuclei.
source: Trophoblast cells are unique to the placenta and perform the majority of its specialized functions. Unsurprisingly, they also make up the largest of the five broad groups of nuclei (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on the clustering data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Clustering of trophoblast nuclei resulted in 13 clusters consisting of 16,386 nuclei.
source: This analysis resulted in 13 clusters consisting of 16,386 nuclei, with clusters ranging in size from 159 to 2906 nuclei (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct report of the clustering analysis results.

claim: The clusters formed five appendages arising from a central body.
source: The clusters formed five appendages arising from a central body.
evidence: This describes the visual organization of clusters in UMAP space.

claim: One cluster in the central body highly expressed the receptor tyrosine kinase Met.
source: One of these clusters highly expressed the receptor tyrosine kinase Met (Figure 2B), which was previously described as a marker of labyrinth trophoblast progenitor (LaTP) cells with trilineage potential: SynTI, SynTII, and S-TGC (Ueno et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study and citation to previous literature.

claim: Met was previously described as a marker of labyrinth trophoblast progenitor cells with trilineage potential: SynTI, SynTII, and S-TGC.
source: One of these clusters highly expressed the receptor tyrosine kinase Met (Figure 2B), which was previously described as a marker of labyrinth trophoblast progenitor (LaTP) cells with trilineage potential: SynTI, SynTII, and S-TGC (Ueno et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The LaTP shared expression of Wnt signaling pathway members Ror2, Lgr5, and Tcf7l1 with presumptive SynTII precursors.
source: Notably, the LaTP shared expression of the Wnt signaling pathway members Ror2, Lgr5, and Tcf7l1 with presumptive SynTII precursors.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study.

claim: A second subpopulation of cells (LaTP2) shared relatively high expression of Tcf7l1 and Pvt1 with LaTPs, but expressed low levels of Met, Ror2, and Lgr5 and high levels of Egfr.
source: Interestingly, the clustering identified a second subpopulation of cells in the central body that shared relatively high expression of Tcf7l1 and the long non-coding RNA Pvt1 with LaTPs, but expressed low levels of Met, Ror2, and Lgr5 and high levels of Egfr (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study.

claim: LaTP2 cells were more closely related to SynTI and S-TGC.
source: These cells were more closely related to SynTI and S-TGC.
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis and UMAP positioning.

claim: Correlative analysis of RNA levels for Met and Egfr in individual cells confirmed that for the most part these markers were uniquely expressed in LaTP and LaTP2 cells, respectively.
source: Correlative analysis of RNA levels for Met and Egfr in individual cells confirmed that for the most part these markers were uniquely expressed in LaTP and LaTP2 cells, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis of gene expression data from the study.

claim: Previously described LaTPs were shown to express high levels of the adhesion protein EPCAM.
source: Previously described LaTPs were also shown to express high levels of the adhesion protein EPCAM (Ueno et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: EPCAM mRNA and protein was mostly limited to the MET+ LaTP cells.
source: EPCAM mRNA and protein was mostly limited to the MET+ LaTP cells, although rare EPCAM/EGFR double positive cells were also present (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is based on RNA expression data and immunofluorescence imaging from the study.

claim: MET expressing LaTP cells were more basal than the EGFR expressing LaTP2 cells.
source: Positionally, MET expressing LaTP cells were more basal than the EGFR expressing LaTP2 cells, suggesting that LaTP may be giving rise to LaTP2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence imaging data from the study.

claim: Immunofluorescence staining of E8.5 embryos identified a large number of EPCAM/MET double positive cells, but few EGFR positive cells in the developing chorion plate.
source: Consistent with this interpretation, immunofluorescence staining of E8.5 embryos identified a large number of EPCAM/MET double positive cells, but few EGFR positive cells in the developing chorion plate (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence imaging data from the study.

claim: LaTPs can be separated into two populations based both on mRNA and protein expression.
source: Together, these data show that LaTPs can be separated into two populations based both on mRNA and protein expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression and immunofluorescence data presented.

claim: The remaining two clusters within the central body appeared to represent precursors of the differentiated cells of the junctional zone – glycogen cells and spongiotrophoblasts.
source: The remaining two clusters within the central body appeared to represent precursors of the differentiated cells of the junctional zone – glycogen cells (GCs) and spongiotrophoblasts (SpT) [Junctional zone precursors (JZPs) 1 and 2 (Figure 2A)].
evidence: This is based on marker gene expression and clustering analysis.

claim: JZP1 exclusively expressed high levels of Cdh4.
source: JZP1 exclusively expressed high levels of Cdh4, whereas Prune2 and Ncam1 showed a continuum of expression, increasing from JZP 1 to 2 and finally specified GCs (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study.

claim: Prune2 and Ncam1 showed a continuum of expression, increasing from JZP 1 to 2 and finally specified GCs.
source: JZP1 exclusively expressed high levels of Cdh4, whereas Prune2 and Ncam1 showed a continuum of expression, increasing from JZP 1 to 2 and finally specified GCs (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data and pseudotime analysis from the study.

claim: The SpT arm separated from late JZP2/early GCs, with increasing expression of Mitf, Flt1, Prl8a9, and Slco2a1 as they transitioned from precursors to differentiated cells.
source: In contrast to GCs, the SpT arm separated from late JZP2/early GCs, with increasing expression of Mitf, Flt1, Prl8a9, and Slco2a1 as they transitioned from precursors to differentiated cells.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data and trajectory analysis from the study.

claim: SynTI was identified based on the expression of known markers including the transferrin receptor Tfrc and monocarboxylase transporter Mct1.
source: SynTI was easily identified based on the expression of known markers of SynTI function including the transferrin receptor Tfrc and monocarboxylase transporter Mct1 (Walentin et al., 2016), but also expressed previously unknown markers such as the transcription factor (TF) Glis1 and the retinol receptor Stra6 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study and citation to previous literature.

claim: SynTI expressed previously unknown markers such as the transcription factor Glis1 and the retinol receptor Stra6.
source: SynTI was easily identified based on the expression of known markers of SynTI function including the transferrin receptor Tfrc and monocarboxylase transporter Mct1 (Walentin et al., 2016), but also expressed previously unknown markers such as the transcription factor (TF) Glis1 and the retinol receptor Stra6 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study.

claim: SynTI precursors expressed high levels of the signaling molecules Epha4 and Tgfa, which decreased with further differentiation.
source: SynTI precursors also expressed these markers, albeit at lower levels, while additionally expressing high levels of the signaling molecules Epha4 and Tgfa, which decreased with further differentiation.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data and pseudotime analysis from the study.

claim: SynTII was annotated by expression of the TF Gcm1 and fusion gene Synb.
source: SynTII was annotated by expression of the TF Gcm1 and fusion gene Synb (Maltepe and Fisher, 2015; Simmons et al., 2008a), but also expressed many previously unknown cell-specific genes such as the glucagon receptor Gcgr and vascular endothelial growth factor Vegfa.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study and citations to previous literature.

claim: SynTII expressed many previously unknown cell-specific genes such as the glucagon receptor Gcgr and vascular endothelial growth factor Vegfa.
source: SynTII was annotated by expression of the TF Gcm1 and fusion gene Synb (Maltepe and Fisher, 2015; Simmons et al., 2008a), but also expressed many previously unknown cell-specific genes such as the glucagon receptor Gcgr and vascular endothelial growth factor Vegfa.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study.

claim: SynTII precursors showed elevated expression of Ror2 and Lgr5 relative to the LaTP.
source: SynTII precursors showed elevated expression of Ror2 and Lgr5 relative to the LaTP.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study.

claim: Tcf7l1 decreased throughout the process of differentiation from LaTP to SynTII.
source: In contrast, Tcf7l1 decreased throughout the process of differentiation from LaTP to SynTII.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data and pseudotime analysis from the study.

claim: S-TGCs were identified by the expression of the canonical marker Ctsq.
source: S-TGCs were easily identified by the expression of the canonical marker Ctsq (Simmons et al., 2007; Simmons et al., 2008a), but also uniquely expressed the leptin receptor Lepr and the Nitric Oxide Synthase one adaptor Nos1ap among other genes.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study and citations to previous literature.

claim: S-TGCs uniquely expressed the leptin receptor Lepr and the Nitric Oxide Synthase one adaptor Nos1ap.
source: S-TGCs were easily identified by the expression of the canonical marker Ctsq (Simmons et al., 2007; Simmons et al., 2008a), but also uniquely expressed the leptin receptor Lepr and the Nitric Oxide Synthase one adaptor Nos1ap among other genes.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study.

claim: Expression of Wnt regulated TF Tcf7l1 along with Wnt receptor Ror2 were maintained from LaTP through commitment to a SynTII precursor state.
source: Expression of Wnt regulated TF Tcf7l1 along with Wnt receptor Ror2 were maintained from LaTP through commitment to a SynTII precursor state.
evidence: This is based on pseudotime analysis of gene expression data from the study.

claim: Upon commitment to the SynTII lineage, the TF Zfhx3 and growth factor receptor Igf1r are newly expressed.
source: Upon commitment to the SynTII lineage, the TF Zfhx3 and growth factor receptor Igf1r are newly expressed while canonical markers Gcm1 and Synb are among the later transcript changes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on pseudotime analysis of gene expression data from the study.

claim: Canonical markers Gcm1 and Synb are among the later transcript changes in SynTII differentiation.
source: Upon commitment to the SynTII lineage, the TF Zfhx3 and growth factor receptor Igf1r are newly expressed while canonical markers Gcm1 and Synb are among the later transcript changes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on pseudotime analysis of gene expression data from the study.

claim: SynTI Precursor cells maintain Pvt1 expression but uniquely upregulate the ephrin receptor Epha4, the Egf-related ligand Tgfa, and the Egf receptor substrate Eps8.
source: SynTI Precursor cells maintain Pvt1 expression but uniquely upregulate the ephrin receptor Epha4, the Egf-related ligand Tgfa, and the Egf receptor substrate Eps8.
evidence: This is based on pseudotime analysis of gene expression data from the study.

claim: Only mature SynTI express the kinase Prkce and clathrin coat assembly protein Snap91.
source: Only mature SynTI express the kinase Prkce and clathrin coat assembly protein Snap91 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on pseudotime analysis of gene expression data from the study.

claim: S-TGC Precursor cells activate the receptors Pparg and Lifr as well as the hypoxia induced TF Epas1 upon lineage commitment.
source: S-TGC Precursor cells activate the receptors Pparg and Lifr as well as the hypoxia induced TF Epas1 upon lineage commitment.
evidence: This is based on pseudotime analysis of gene expression data from the study.

claim: Expression of the canonical marker Ctsq occurs only in mature S-TGC along with Lepr and the glucocorticoid signaling effector Tsc22d3.
source: Expression of the canonical marker Ctsq occurs only in mature S-TGC along with Lepr and the glucocorticoid signaling effector Tsc22d3 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is based on pseudotime analysis of gene expression data from the study.

claim: The data are consistent with distinct signaling pathways (SynTII – WNT, IGF; SynTI – EGF, EPH; S-TGC – LIF, PPAR) driving differentiation of LaTP into the three main cell types of the placental labyrinth.
source: These data are consistent with distinct signaling pathways (e.g. SynTII – WNT, IGF; SynTI – EGF, EPH; S-TGC – LIF, PPAR) driving differentiation of LaTP into the three main cell types of the placental labyrinth.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the pseudotime analysis of gene expression data.

claim: The S-TGC appear to differentiate from the junction of LaTP2 and JZP1.
source: Interestingly, the S-TGC appear to differentiate from the junction of LaTP2 and JZP1 (Figure 2A), potentially suggestive that S-TGC arise from ectoplacental cone cells (Simmons et al., 2007; Simmons et al., 2008a) as well as from chorion derived LaTP (Ueno et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on the clustering and UMAP positioning of S-TGC cells.

claim: Immunofluorescence of the representative markers NCAM1 and SLCO2A1 confirmed their expression in the JZ.
source: Immunofluorescence of the representative markers NCAM1 and SLCO2A1 confirmed their expression in the JZ (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence imaging data from the study.

claim: Staining of juxtaposed sections confirmed the mutually exclusive expression of NCAM1 and SLCO2A1.
source: Furthermore, staining of juxtaposed sections confirmed their mutually exclusive expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence imaging data from the study.

claim: Co-staining with the known GC marker PCDH12 verified the GC identity of the NCAM1+ cells.
source: Co-staining with the known GC marker PCDH12 (Rampon et al., 2005), verified the GC identity of the NCAM1+ cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence imaging data from the study and citation to previous literature.

claim: Expression analysis of prolactin genes showed both distinct and overlapping expression of this large gene family between the SpT and GC cells.
source: Expression analysis of prolactin genes showed both distinct and overlapping expression of this large gene family between the SpT and GC cells, and confirmed the identities of these clusters (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study.

claim: Parietal TGC nuclei were not identified in the snRNA-seq data, likely due to their very large size precluding their passage through the FACS pre-filter.
source: Of important note, parietal TGC nuclei were not identified in our snRNA-seq data, likely due to their very large size precluding their passage through the FACS pre-filter, which removes nuclei greater than 35 microns (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of parietal TGC in the data and knowledge of their size.

claim: The data did not identify invasive trophoblast giant cells that invade the decidua, which was dissected away.
source: Our data also did not identify invasive trophoblast giant cells (spiral artery and canal TGCs) that invade the decidua, which was dissected away.
evidence: This explains the absence of certain cell types based on the dissection method used.

claim: The LaTP populations rapidly diminished over time, resulting in few progenitors remaining by E14.5.
source: This visualization clearly showed the rapid diminishment of the LaTP populations over time, resulting in few progenitors remaining by E14.5 (Figure 3A and B, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is based on analysis of cell population proportions across developmental timepoints.

claim: The precursor populations decreased over time, presumably maturing into terminally differentiated cells, which dramatically increased during the time course.
source: The precursor populations also decreased over time, presumably maturing into terminally differentiated cells, which dramatically increased during the time course (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is based on analysis of cell population proportions across developmental timepoints.

claim: The majority of Mki67 expressing nuclei were among the progenitor and precursor cell populations.
source: The majority of Mki67 expressing nuclei were among the progenitor and precursor cell populations (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on analysis of Mki67 expression across cell populations.

claim: At E9.5 and E10.5, a substantial number of nuclei at the distal tips of each arm also expressed Mki67, suggesting ongoing proliferation even after cells have transitioned to a more mature-like expression state.
source: However, at E9.5 and E10.5, a substantial number of nuclei at the distal tips of each arm also expressed Mki67, suggesting ongoing proliferation even after cells have transitioned to a more mature-like expression state.
evidence: This is based on analysis of Mki67 expression across cell populations and developmental timepoints.

claim: Very few nuclei expressed Mki67 at E14.5 consistent with the expansion in placental cell number happening prior to E14.5.
source: Very few nuclei expressed Mki67 at E14.5 consistent with the expansion in placental cell number happening prior to E14.5, with later growth occurring through cellular hypertrophy rather than cell division (Ueno et al., 2013; Paikari et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on analysis of Mki67 expression at E14.5 and citations to previous literature.

claim: Progenitor vectors (LaTP and LaTP2) showed little directionality and small magnitudes, likely reflecting a maintenance of multipotency and self-renewal.
source: Progenitor vectors (LaTP and LaTP2) showed little directionality and small magnitudes, likely reflecting a maintenance of multipotency and self-renewal.
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis and represents an inference about progenitor cell behavior.

claim: The cells within each precursor population showed uniform directionality and large magnitudes, especially at E10.5 and E12.5, the period of greatest placental expansion.
source: In contrast, the cells within each precursor population showed uniform directionality and large magnitudes, especially at E10.5 and E12.5, the period of greatest placental expansion.
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis.

claim: The differentiated cell populations showed vectors of great magnitude and uniform directionality at the early timepoints, suggesting ongoing transcriptional maturation, before diminishing by E14.5.
source: Surprisingly, the differentiated cell populations also showed vectors of great magnitude and uniform directionality at the early timepoints, suggesting ongoing transcriptional maturation, before diminishing by E14.5.
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis and represents an inference about ongoing maturation.

claim: The number of differentially expressed genes in S-TGC at each consecutive timepoint increased from 143 to 700 genes.
source: Consistent with the vectors, the number of differentially expressed genes at each consecutive timepoint increased from 143 to 700 genes (adj. p-value<0.05; Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, Figure 3—source datas 2–4).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis of S-TGC across timepoints.

claim: Genes up at E9.5 in S-TGC were highly enriched for ontology groups concerning cell division.
source: Gene ontology analysis showed that genes up at E9.5 were highly enriched for ontology groups concerning cell division, while those at E14.5 were enriched for Ras GTPase signaling and various developmental processes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on gene ontology analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Genes up at E14.5 in S-TGC were enriched for Ras GTPase signaling and various developmental processes.
source: Gene ontology analysis showed that genes up at E9.5 were highly enriched for ontology groups concerning cell division, while those at E14.5 were enriched for Ras GTPase signaling and various developmental processes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on gene ontology analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Examples of genes that increased over developmental time in S-TGC include Ctsq, the Cathepsins, and several genes involved in hormone signaling and response.
source: Examples of genes that increased over developmental time include Ctsq, the Cathepsins (Ctsj, Ctsr, Ctsm, Cts3, and Cts6), and several genes involved in hormone signaling and response (Lepr, Tsc22d3, and Ghrh) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,D,E,F).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis across timepoints.

claim: Podxl is expressed from the very early stages of S-TGC specification through E14.5.
source: In contrast, Podxl is expressed from the very early stages of S-TGC specification through E14.5.
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis across timepoints.

claim: Podxl is a highly charged membrane protein which has been implicated in luminogenesis in early embryos.
source: Podxl is a highly charged membrane protein which, in a different context, has been implicated in luminogenesis in early embryos (Shahbazi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The early expression of Podxl in S-TGCs might function in maintaining open maternal blood spaces within the placental labyrinth.
source: While the formation of maternal blood spaces in the placental is distinct from the early embryo, the early expression of Podxl in S-TGCs might function in maintaining open maternal blood spaces within the placental labyrinth.
evidence: This is speculation based on the known function of Podxl in other contexts and its expression pattern in S-TGC.

claim: The differential dynamics of PODXL and LEPR in S-TGCs was confirmed by immunohistochemistry.
source: The differential dynamics of PODXL and LEPR in S-TGCs was confirmed by immunohistochemistry (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemistry imaging data from the study.

claim: Similar ongoing maturation processes were seen in the SynTII, SynTI, GC, and SpT populations.
source: Similar ongoing maturation processes were seen in the SynTII, SynTI, GC, and SpT populations (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis across timepoints for multiple cell types.

claim: The data support a model of early expansion by self-renewing progenitor cells and committed precursors followed by ongoing maturation of all five differentiated cell types of the placenta proper.
source: Together these data support a model of early expansion by self-renewing progenitor cells and committed precursors followed by ongoing maturation of all five differentiated cell types of the placenta proper.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RNA velocity and differential expression analyses.

claim: Fetal and maternal blood are separated by a thin membrane consisting of four cell layers starting with the fetal endothelial cells, then SynTII, followed by SynTI, and finally S-TGCs.
source: Fetal and maternal blood are separated by a thin membrane consisting of four cell layers starting with the fetal endothelial cells, then SynTII, followed by SynTI, and finally S-TGCs (Simmons et al., 2008a; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature and reference to Figure 4A.

claim: A basal lamina separates the fetal endothelial cells from SynTII cells.
source: A basal lamina separates the fetal endothelial cells from SynTII cells.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about the structure of the gas exchange interface.

claim: Immunohistochemistry for the marker genes PECAM1, IGF1R, STRA6, and PODXL demonstrate each cluster corresponds to endothelial, SynTII, SynTI, and S-TGC populations respectively in vivo.
source: Immunohistochemistry for the marker genes PECAM1, IGF1R, STRA6, and PODXL demonstrate each cluster corresponds to endothelial, SynTII, SynTI, and S-TGC populations respectively in vivo (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemistry imaging data from the study.

claim: PODXL+ cytoplasmic extensions of the S-TGCs spread over the perimeter of the maternal blood space forming a permeable lining.
source: PODXL+ cytoplasmic extensions of the S-TGCs spread over the perimeter of the maternal blood space forming a permeable lining (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on high-resolution immunofluorescence imaging data from the study.

claim: SynTII differentially expressed genes were highly enriched for cell–cell and cell–matrix interactions such as those encoding cell junction and cell adherens proteins.
source: SynTII differentially expressed genes were highly enriched for cell–cell and cell–matrix interactions such as those encoding cell junction and cell adherens proteins consistent with a role as a basal permeability barrier between maternal and fetal blood.
evidence: This is based on gene ontology analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: SynTII expressed collagens and laminin subunits, which likely form the basal lamina separating SynTII from the fetal endothelium.
source: SynTII also expressed collagens and laminin subunits (Figure 4E), which likely form the basal lamina separating SynTII from the fetal endothelium.
evidence: This is based on gene expression data and represents an inference about the function of these proteins.

claim: SynTI differentially expressed genes were enriched for intracellular transport and cell signaling including genes encoding for vesicular organization and transport, protein localization to membranes, and Ras signaling.
source: In contrast, SynTI differentially expressed genes were enriched for intracellular transport and cell signaling including genes encoding for vesicular organization and transport, protein localization to membranes, and Ras signaling.
evidence: This is based on gene ontology analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: The data are consistent with SynTI layer playing a critical role in the transport of materials between maternal and fetal blood.
source: These data are consistent with SynTI layer playing a critical role in the transport of materials between maternal and fetal blood.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the gene ontology analysis.

claim: SynTI is enriched for genes involved in neuron projection development, driven by expression of canonical axonal pathfinding genes and synapse genes.
source: SynTI is also enriched for genes involved in neuron projection development, driven by expression of canonical axonal pathfinding genes (Plxna2, Plxnd1) and synapse genes (Snap91).
evidence: This is based on gene ontology analysis and gene expression data.

claim: The S-TGC were enriched for GTPase and Ras signaling and receptors including Kras, Grb2, and Pdgfrb.
source: Although more generally understood as an exocrine cell type, the S-TGC were enriched for GTPase and Ras signaling and receptors including Kras, Grb2, and Pdgfrb, suggesting these cells also transduce signals from maternal blood.
evidence: This is based on gene ontology analysis and gene expression data.

claim: S-TGC differentially expressed genes were strikingly enriched for those encoding for migration factors.
source: S-TGC differentially expressed genes were strikingly enriched for those encoding for migration factors.
evidence: This is based on gene ontology analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: S-TGC expression of migration factors could explain the long thin cellular extensions from these cells, which form the only non-syncytial trophoblast at the interface.
source: Such expression could explain the long thin cellular extensions from these cells, which form the only non-syncytial trophoblast at the interface (Coan et al., 2005).
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression data and citation to previous literature about S-TGC morphology.

claim: S-TGCs are connected to SynTI by desmosomes, which are known to undergo constant remodeling and have additional functions in signaling and migration.
source: S-TGCs are connected to SynTI by desmosomes, which are known to undergo constant remodeling and have additional functions in signaling and migration (Simmons et al., 2008a; Johnson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The results suggested a striking separation of functions between the trophoblast layers.
source: The results suggested a striking separation of functions between the layers (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of solute transporter and vitamin/cholesterol transport gene expression.

claim: Genes responsible for carboxylate transport were highly enriched in SynTII, while organic anion transporters were enriched in SynTI.
source: For example, genes responsible for carboxylate transport were highly enriched in SynTII, while organic anion transporters were enriched in SynTI.
evidence: This is based on analysis of solute transporter gene expression across cell types.

claim: Factors important in Zinc transport were distributed across, yet distinctly expressed between the populations.
source: Even within specific transport pathways, functions were often separated; for example, factors important in Zinc transport were distributed across, yet distinctly expressed between the populations.
evidence: This is based on analysis of solute transporter gene expression across cell types.

claim: Cholesterol transporters are enriched in SynTII (Scarb1, Vldlr) and S-TGC (Hdlbp, Ldlr).
source: Cholesterol transporters are enriched in SynTII (Scarb1, Vldlr) and S-TGC (Hdlbp, Ldlr), while Folate receptors (Folr1, Folr2) are uniquely expressed in SynTI.
evidence: This is based on analysis of cholesterol and vitamin transport gene expression across cell types.

claim: Folate receptors (Folr1, Folr2) are uniquely expressed in SynTI.
source: Cholesterol transporters are enriched in SynTII (Scarb1, Vldlr) and S-TGC (Hdlbp, Ldlr), while Folate receptors (Folr1, Folr2) are uniquely expressed in SynTI.
evidence: This is based on analysis of vitamin transport gene expression across cell types.

claim: The data show a highly evolved separation of functions between the three trophoblast layers that separate maternal from fetal blood.
source: Together, these data show a highly evolved separation of functions between the three trophoblast layers that separate maternal from fetal blood.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of transporter gene expression across cell types.

claim: A total of 139 unique ligand–receptor interactions reaching significance were uncovered by CellPhoneDB analysis.
source: A total of 139 unique ligand–receptor interactions reaching significance (adj. p-value<0.05) were uncovered.
evidence: This is a direct report of the CellPhoneDB analysis results.

claim: CellPhoneDB predicted an interaction between Rspo3 in the endothelium with Lgr5 in the LaTP/SynTII lineage.
source: CellPhoneDB predicted an interaction between Rspo3 in the endothelium with Lgr5 in the LaTP/SynTII lineage (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is based on CellPhoneDB analysis of ligand-receptor interactions.

claim: Rspo3 is required in vivo for the maintenance of Gcm1 expression.
source: Rspo3 is required in vivo for the maintenance of Gcm1 expression (Kazanskaya et al., 2008; Aoki et al., 2007) and canonical Wnt signaling is essential for differentiation of SynTII (Zhu et al., 2017; Matsuura et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Canonical Wnt signaling is essential for differentiation of SynTII.
source: Rspo3 is required in vivo for the maintenance of Gcm1 expression (Kazanskaya et al., 2008; Aoki et al., 2007) and canonical Wnt signaling is essential for differentiation of SynTII (Zhu et al., 2017; Matsuura et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Predicted signaling in the opposite direction included Vegfa secreted by SynTII to the receptors Kdr, Flt1, Nrp1, Nrp2 located only on endothelial cells.
source: Predicted signaling in the opposite direction included Vegfa secreted by SynTII to the receptors Kdr, Flt1, Nrp1, Nrp2 located only on endothelial cells.
evidence: This is based on CellPhoneDB analysis of ligand-receptor interactions.

claim: Immunostaining confirmed SynTII and SynTI as the sources of VEGFA in the labyrinth.
source: Immunostaining confirmed SynTII and SynTI as the sources of VEGFA in the labyrinth (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 5–S2A).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence imaging data from the study.

claim: The data suggest a feedback loop where Rspo3-Lgr5 supports SynTII differentiation and function, while Vegfa-Kdr/Flt1 drives vascular maintenance and remodeling.
source: These data suggest a feedback loop where Rspo3-Lgr5 supports SynTII differentiation and function, while Vegfa-Kdr/Flt1 drives vascular maintenance and remodeling, thereby coordinating lineage differentiation with development of tissue structure.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the CellPhoneDB analysis and immunostaining data.

claim: CellPhoneDB analysis predicted an interaction between the EGFR ligands Tgfa, Hbegf, and Nrg1 produced by SynTI with Egfr on both LaTP2 and SynTI precursor populations.
source: CellPhoneDB analysis was consistent with that interpretation as it predicted an interaction between the EGFR ligands Tgfa, Hbegf, and Nrg1 produced by SynTI with Egfr on both LaTP2 and SynTI precursor populations.
evidence: This is based on CellPhoneDB analysis of ligand-receptor interactions.

claim: CellPhoneDB predicted an interaction between EGFR ligands and Egfr on LaTP, SynTII, and S-TGCs.
source: However, it also predicted an interaction with Egfr on LaTP, SynTII, and S-TGCs (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is based on CellPhoneDB analysis of ligand-receptor interactions.

claim: Protein expression confirmed HBEGF alone in SynTI, and colocalization of HBEGF and EGFR in SynTII.
source: We confirmed protein expression HBEGF alone in SynTI, and colocalization of HBEGF and EGFR in SynTII (Figure 5D; Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence imaging data from the study.

claim: SynTI appears to be a hub of EGF signaling that impacts the majority of the cell populations in the labyrinth.
source: Therefore, SynTI appears to be a hub of EGF signaling that impacts the majority of the cell populations in the labyrinth.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the CellPhoneDB analysis and immunostaining data.

claim: Loss of Egfr in vivo results in decreased placental size, disorganized labyrinth, and a reduction in the SpT layer.
source: Loss of Egfr in vivo results in decreased placental size, disorganized labyrinth, and a reduction in the SpT layer (Du et al., 2004; Miettinen et al., 1995; Strunk et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Numerous ligand–receptor interactions between Bmp8a and several receptors, including Acvr1, Bmpr1, and Bmpr2 were predicted in the labyrinth.
source: Numerous ligand–receptor interactions between Bmp8a and several receptors, including Acvr1, Bmpr1, and Bmpr2 were predicted in the labyrinth.
evidence: This is based on CellPhoneDB analysis of ligand-receptor interactions.

claim: The source of Bmp8a is LaTP and SynTII and the receptors are located on all labyrinth populations.
source: The source of Bmp8a is LaTP and SynTII and the receptors are located on all labyrinth populations, including LaTP and SynTII (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is based on CellPhoneDB analysis and gene expression data.

claim: Bmp7 is secreted by LaTP and Bmp6 by the endothelium.
source: Bmp7 is secreted by LaTP and Bmp6 by the endothelium (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study.

claim: Smad1/3/5/6 displayed varied levels of expression across trophoblast populations.
source: Smad2/4/7 were relatively uniformly expressed in trophoblasts, while Smad1/3/5/6 displayed varied levels of expression across trophoblast populations (Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is based on gene expression data from the study.

claim: Loss of Smad1, and combined knockout of Bmp5/7 exhibit severe placental defects.
source: Previous work has shown that while Bmp8a is largely redundant with Bmp8b, loss of Smad1, and combined knockout of Bmp5/7 exhibit severe placental defects (Zhao and Hogan, 1996; Tremblay et al., 2001; Solloway and Robertson, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Application of SCENIC to the trophoblast dataset recovered 200 transcription factor regulons with activity in at least one cluster.
source: Application of SCENIC to the trophoblast dataset recovered 200 transcription factor regulons with activity in at least one cluster (Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is a direct report of the SCENIC analysis results.

claim: There was overall strong agreement between UMAP projections based on transcript expression and regulon activity.
source: There was overall strong agreement in the two approaches to separate nuclei by cell type both in UMAP space and hierarchical clustering of Pearson correlations between populations (Figure 2A vs. Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on comparison of UMAP projections and correlation analyses.

claim: TF regulon activity provides an alternative means to identify the different cell types of the placenta.
source: These data show that TF regulon activity provides an alternative means to identify the different cell types of the placenta.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of transcript-based and regulon-based clustering.

claim: The identified regulons with differential activity across the populations included both known and unknown TF regulators of placental development.
source: The identified regulons with differential activity across the populations included both known and unknown TF regulators of placental development.
evidence: This is a summary of the SCENIC analysis results.

claim: Known factors include Gcm1 in SynTII specification, Grhl2 in S-TGC, and Ets2 in JZ development.
source: Known factors include Gcm1 in SynTII specification, Grhl2 in S-TGC, and Ets2 in JZ development (Figure 6B; Anson-Cartwright et al., 2000; Walentin et al., 2015; Yamamoto et al., 1998).
evidence: This is based on SCENIC analysis and citations to previous literature.

claim: Examples of unknown regulators include Tbx15 in LaTP, Gata1 in SynTII, Pax2 in SynTI, and Meis1 in S-TGC.
source: Examples of the many unknowns include Tbx15 in LaTP, Gata1 in SynTII, Pax2 in SynTI, and Meis1 in S-TGC.
evidence: This is based on SCENIC analysis identifying novel regulons.

claim: While expression of Gcm1 and Pax8 correlated the distribution of their regulon activity, Ets2 and Esrrg did not.
source: While expression of Gcm1 and Pax8 correlated the distribution of their regulon activity, Ets2 and Esrrg did not.
evidence: This is based on comparison of TF expression and regulon activity distributions.

claim: Ets2 was broadly expressed, yet its regulon activity was highly enriched among differentiating S-TGCs and GCs.
source: Ets2 was broadly expressed, yet its regulon activity was highly enriched among differentiating S-TGCs and GCs.
evidence: This is based on comparison of TF expression and regulon activity distributions.

claim: Esrrg was lowly expressed throughout, yet showed strong regulon active among SpT cells.
source: Esrrg, on the other hand, was lowly expressed throughout, yet showed strong regulon active among SpT cells.
evidence: This is based on comparison of TF expression and regulon activity distributions.

claim: Esrrg has known roles in steroid hormone production and metabolism in human trophoblast.
source: Esrrg is not well studied in the mouse placenta, but has known roles in steroid hormone production and metabolism in human trophoblast, functions also important in the mouse placenta (Poidatz et al., 2012; Luo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Only 17 of the 200 TFs had annotated placental phenotypes, while 124 are lethal during development.
source: Only 17 of the 200 TFs had annotated placental phenotypes, while 124 are lethal during development (defined as until weaning) (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the Mouse Genome Informatic database.

claim: 68% of 103 intrauterine lethal and subviable mouse knockout lines also have placental defects.
source: Many of these developmental lethal phenotypes likely are associated with placental defects given that 68% of 103 intrauterine lethal and subviable mouse knockout lines also have placental defects (Perez-Garcia et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Gcm1 and Zhfx3 have reciprocal high confidence motif in their promoter regions, suggestive of a positive feedback loop.
source: Gcm1, the master regulator of the SynTI lineage, and Zhfx3 have reciprocal high confidence motif in their promoter regions, suggestive of a positive feedback loop.
evidence: This is based on SCENIC analysis of TF binding motifs and represents an inference about regulatory relationships.

claim: Zfhx3 and Tcf7l2 show mutual regulation of one another, and Tcf7l2 also has a high confidence binding site in the promoter of Gcm1.
source: Zfhx3 and Tcf7l2 also show mutual regulation of one another, and Tcf7l2 also has a high confidence binding site in the promoter of Gcm1.
evidence: This is based on SCENIC analysis of TF binding motifs.

claim: Two independent genetic disruptions of Zfhx3 result in embryonic to pre-weaning lethality with surviving pups exhibiting severe growth defects.
source: Zfhx3 (Atbf1) does not have known functions in the placenta. However, two independent genetic disruptions of Zfhx3 result in embryonic to pre-weaning lethality with surviving pups exhibiting severe growth defects (Sun et al., 2012; Parsons et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: High confidence motifs for Tcf7l2 were identified in the promoter regions of many genes important for SynTII differentiation and function including Lgr5, Vegfa, Slc43a2, and Gcm1.
source: While Tcf7l2 knockout mice do not have a placental phenotype, we identify high confidence motifs in the promoter regions of many genes important for SynTII differentiation and function including Lgr5, Vegfa, Slc43a2, and Gcm1 (Perez-Garcia et al., 2018; Kazanskaya et al., 2008; Guetg et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on SCENIC analysis of TF binding motifs and citations to previous literature.

claim: It is possible that redundancy with Tcf7l1 underlies the lack of Tcf7l2 knockout placental phenotype.
source: It is possible that redundancy with Tcf7l1 underlies the lack of Tcf7l2 knockout placental phenotype (Nguyen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is speculation based on known redundancy between these factors and citation to previous literature.

claim: Gata1 has high confidence binding sites in the promoter of multiple genes with important functions in SynTII including Vegfa, Slc40a1, and Trp63.
source: While Gata1 has not been studied in the context of the mouse placenta, transcript expression, regulon activity, and high confidence motifs suggest it regulates multiple genes with important functions in SynTII including Vegfa, Slc40a1 (ferroportin), and the basal epithelial transcription factor Trp63.
evidence: This is based on SCENIC analysis of TF binding motifs and gene expression data.

claim: Immunofluorescence showed the colocalization of GATA1 with IGFR1, thereby confirming its expression in SynTII.
source: Immunofluorescence showed the colocalization of GATA1 with IGFR1, thereby confirming its expression in SynTII (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence imaging data from the study.

claim: Strong GATA1 protein expression was visible in the SynTII nuclei abutting the basal membrane, but not in SynTI nuclei closest to maternal blood spaces.
source: In particular, strong GATA1 protein expression was visible in the SynTII nuclei abutting the basal membrane (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D – white arrow heads), but not in SynTI nuclei closest to maternal blood spaces (Figure 6F – yellow arrowhead).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence imaging data from the study.

claim: GATA1 appears to be expressed exclusively in SynTII population of trophoblasts and likely has important regulatory functions specific to SynTII.
source: Therefore, GATA1 appears to be expressed exclusively in SynTII population of trophoblasts and likely has important regulatory functions specific to SynTII.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunofluorescence data and SCENIC analysis.

claim: Almost 30% of trophoblast nuclei captured in this study originate from SynT cells.
source: In contrast to previous studies where SynT comprise fewer than 10% of cells identified, almost 30% of trophoblast nuclei captured in this study originate from SynT cells.
evidence: This is based on quantification of cell type proportions in the dataset.

claim: Profiling four developmental stages from E9.5 to E14.5 allowed for the capture of stem/progenitor and terminally differentiated populations including previously unknown intermediate states.
source: Profiling four developmental stages from E9.5 to E14.5 allowed for the capture of stem/progenitor and terminally differentiated populations including previously unknown intermediate states and new putative regulators of cell identity.
evidence: This is a summary of the study design and findings.

claim: Modeling receptor–ligand interactions predicted how SynTII and endothelial cells coordinate spatial proximity and development through growth factor secretion.
source: Modeling receptor–ligand interactions predicted how SynTII and endothelial cells coordinate spatial proximity and development through growth factor secretion.
evidence: This is a summary of the CellPhoneDB analysis findings.

claim: Network inference predicted gene regulatory networks defined by TFs and feedback loops among the TFs, including novel candidate regulators of placental development.
source: In addition, network inference predicted gene regulatory networks defined by TFs and feedback loops among the TFs, including novel candidate regulators of placental development.
evidence: This is a summary of the SCENIC analysis findings.

claim: The relationship between LaTP and LaTP2 populations is unclear.
source: The relationship between these populations is unclear.
evidence: This acknowledges uncertainty about the developmental relationship between these populations.

claim: Both LaTP populations had low RNA velocities and there was no coordinated directionality to indicate differentiation from one population to the other.
source: Both LaTP populations had low RNA velocities and there was no coordinated directionality to indicate differentiation from one population to the other.
evidence: This is based on RNA velocity analysis.

claim: The relative positions of the two populations in the developing labyrinth and the earlier presence of EPCAM/MET double positive cells suggest that LaTP2 arise from LaTP.
source: However, the relative positions of the two populations in the developing labyrinth and the earlier presence of EPCAM/MET double positive cells (i.e. at E8.5) suggest that LaTP2 arise from LaTP.
evidence: This is an inference based on spatial positioning and temporal expression data.

claim: The two LaTP populations may arise from progenitors that separate earlier in development resulting in distinct lineage biases.
source: Alternatively, the two populations may arise from progenitors that separate earlier in development resulting in distinct lineage biases.
evidence: This is speculation about an alternative developmental relationship.

claim: LaTP is more similar to SynTII, while LaTP2 is more similar to SynTI and S-TGC.
source: LaTP is more similar to SynTII, while LaTP2 is more similar to SynTI and S-TGC.
evidence: This is based on clustering analysis and UMAP positioning.

claim: Understanding the specification and heterogeneity of labyrinth progenitors will be an important undertaking given that early defects are likely to have large effects in proportion of terminally differentiated trophoblast.
source: Understanding the specification and heterogeneity of labyrinth progenitors will be an important undertaking given that early defects are likely to have large effects in proportion of terminally differentiated trophoblast resulting in embryonic defects and ultimately reduced viability.
evidence: This is speculation about the importance of future research based on inference about developmental consequences.

claim: Profiling differentiation to SynTII confirmed previous work demonstrating the role of Wnt signaling in specification and efficient differentiation of SynTII, both in vivo and in vitro.
source: Profiling differentiation to SynTII confirmed previous work demonstrating the role of Wnt signaling in specification and efficient differentiation of SynTII, both in vivo and in vitro (Zhu et al., 2017; Matsuura et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on pseudotime analysis from the study and citations to previous literature.

claim: Detailed information and derivation protocols did not exist for SynTI or S-TGC prior to this study.
source: However, such detailed information and derivation protocols did not exist for SynTI or S-TGC.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to this study.

claim: Expression of Egf ligands by mature SynTI and Egfr by LaTP 2, SynTII, and S-TGC underscore the centrality of Egf signaling to labyrinth development and function.
source: Additionally, expression of Egf ligands by mature SynTI and Egfr by LaTP 2, SynTII, and S-TGC underscore the centrality of Egf signaling to labyrinth development and function.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the gene expression data.

claim: Deciphering the mechanism of Egfr loss has been confounded by defects in junctional zone cells and strain-specific variation.
source: While Egfr loss or mutation in vivo causes labyrinth disorganization, the deciphering of mechanism has been confounded by defects in junctional zone cells and strain-specific variation (Du et al., 2004; Strunk et al., 2004; Dackor et al., 2009; Lee and Threadgill, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In human trophoblast, EGF has been shown to stimulate differentiation to SynT in vitro.
source: In human trophoblast, EGF has been shown to stimulate differentiation to SynT in vitro and decreased EGFR phosphorylation is associated with intrauterine growth restriction (Morrish et al., 1987; Fondacci et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Decreased EGFR phosphorylation is associated with intrauterine growth restriction.
source: In human trophoblast, EGF has been shown to stimulate differentiation to SynT in vitro and decreased EGFR phosphorylation is associated with intrauterine growth restriction (Morrish et al., 1987; Fondacci et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A careful temporal and cell-type-specific dissection of the loss of Egfr will be necessary to separate the multiple functions of Egf signaling in placental development and health.
source: Given the redundancy of Egf ligands, a careful temporal and cell-type-specific dissection of the loss of Egfr will be necessary to separate the multiple functions of Egf signaling in placental development and health.
evidence: This is speculation about future research needs based on the complexity of Egf signaling.

claim: Pseudotemporal ordering along the S-TGC trajectory implicated Lif-Stat3 signaling evidenced by increasing expression of Lifr and supported by high activity of the predicted Stat3 regulon.
source: Pseudotemporal ordering along the S-TGC trajectory implicated Lif-Stat3 signaling evidenced by increasing expression of Lifr and supported by high activity of the predicted Stat3 regulon by SCENIC.
evidence: This is based on pseudotime analysis and SCENIC analysis.

claim: Loss of Lifr results in disorganization of the labyrinth and dramatically enlarged non-functional maternal blood sinuses lined by multinuclear aggregates, and not S-TGC.
source: Loss of Lifr results in disorganization of the labyrinth and dramatically enlarged non-functional maternal blood sinuses lined by multinuclear aggregates, and not S-TGC (Ware et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: This striking labyrinth phenotype is likely explained by a necessity for Lif signaling in the differentiation, patterning, and/or function of S-TGC.
source: While Lif-Stat3 is also active in the junctional zone, this striking labyrinth phenotype is likely explained by a necessity for Lif signaling in the differentiation, patterning, and/or function of S-TGC.
